convention: clang -fobjc-arc -O2 -o nax_load_ab nax_load_ab.m -framework Metal -framework Foundation; compiles MSL at RUNTIME (MTLLanguageVersion4_0, fast-math for the tensor arm), no Python / no MetalHLO / no torch / no MLX runtime in the path; arms: steel = MLX steel gemm_loop read from --metal (default ./nax_steel_gemm.metal, must sit beside the binary) and shader = naive exact-fp32 fma control; ./nax_load_ab --arm steel|shader --shape M N K --reps R --burst B [--seconds S] [--samples N] [--tol F]; prints a row ONLY if the sampled CPU oracle and the non-zero-output check pass, so a silent no-op cannot produce a number. steel requires M%64==N%128==K%256==0.
evidence: 2026-10-15 (window: omlx=down, headless, idle floor 40/84 mW): steel 275.0 us/GEMM = 7808 GFLOPS @50.2 W = 13.8 mJ/GEMM vs shader 2561.2 us = 838 GFLOPS @71.6 W = 183.3 mJ/GEMM, both oracle-PASS with maxabs=0 at 1024^3. Capture: results/EXP-029-nax-crosslane/results/nax_baremetal-energy-20261015T145713Z.txt. Against the optimized Steel64 SIMT arm the ratio is 2.3x (mlx-comparison, 4096^2).
purpose: nax_load_ab.m — EXP-029: BARE-METAL matched A/B for the tensor-unit (NAX) datapath: compiles the real MLX steel gemm_loop and a matched SIMT control at runtime, gates both on a CPU oracle, and measures per-GEMM time and GPU energy without any stacked library.
